source.author: lucan
source.text: Postquam discessit Olympo Herculea gravis Ossa manu, subitaeque ruinam Sensit aquae Nereus: melius mansura sub undis, Emathis aequorei regnum Pharsalos Achillis Eminet, et, prima Rhoeteia litora pinu Quae tetigit, Phylace, Pteleosque, et Dorion ira Flebile Pieridum; Trachin, pretioque nefandae Lampados Herculeis fortis Meliboea pharetris: Atque olim Larissa potens: ubi nobile quondam Nunc super Argos arant: veteres ubi fabula Thebas Monstrat Echionias: ubi quondam Pentheos exsul Colla caputque ferens supremo tradidit igni, Questa, quod hoc solum nato rapuisset, Agave.
source.text_original: Postquam discessit Olympo / Herculea gravis Ossa manu, subitaeque ruinam / Sensit aquae Nereus: melius mansura sub undis, / Emathis aequorei regnum Pharsalos Achillis / Eminet, et, prima Rhoeteia litora pinu / Quae tetigit, Phylace, Pteleosque, et Dorion ira / Flebile Pieridum; Trachin, pretioque nefandae / Lampados Herculeis fortis Meliboea pharetris: / Atque olim Larissa potens: ubi nobile quondam / Nunc super Argos arant: veteres ubi fabula Thebas / Monstrat Echionias: ubi quondam Pentheos exsul / Colla caputque ferens supremo tradidit igni, / Questa, quod hoc solum nato rapuisset, Agave.
source.text_english: After Ossa, burdened by Hercules’ hand, withdrew from Olympus, and Nereus felt the sudden collapse of the waters: the kingdom of the sea is better left beneath the waves. Emathia’s Pharsalos, Achilles’ Pharsalos, stands forth; and Phylace, first touched by the Rhoetean pine, and Pteleos, and Dorion, lamented by the Pierides for their wrath; Trachin, and Meliboea, strong with Hercules’ quivers, bought at the price of the accursed torch; and once-powerful Larissa, where now they plough over ancient Argos; where the old tale shows Echionian Thebes; where Pentheus, once an exile, bearing his neck and head, surrendered to the final fire, as Agave complained that this alone had been snatched from her son.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nititur hinc Talaus fratrisque Leodocus urget remo terga sui, quos nobile contulit Argos.
reuse.text_original: nititur hinc Talaus fratrisque Leodocus urget / remo terga sui, quos nobile contulit Argos.
reuse.text_english: From this side Talaus presses on, and Leodocus drives with his oar the backs of his brother’s men, whom noble Argos had brought together.
